submission.justification: PROVISIONAL. No document or tool gives humidity-ageing data for any candidate, so the hard transparency constraint (≤10% loss after 10-year-equivalent ageing) is unverified for all three. R3 separates best (about 4.5 sigma at 2 cm), but it is a high-index porous radiator with no moisture protection documented. R1 is porous with a hydrophobic treatment, which makes it the most plausible porous option to pass. It gives about 3.8 sigma at 3 cm, its simulated optimum (2 cm: 3.68, 3 cm: 3.78, 4 cm: 3.50, 6 cm: 2.85). Separation falls at large thickness for every radiator. I chose R1 over R3 to avoid risking an irreversible failure of the hard requirement. Humidity-ageing results must be confirmed for R1 before procurement. If R3 passes the ageing test, it would be the better choice, at about 2 cm. The vessel is flushed with dry nitrogen, which may reduce the humidity exposure, but this does not replace the ageing test.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates

requirements.evidence: No ageing data in any document. R1's hydrophobic treatment is only indirect support. The vessel is dry-N2 flushed.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R1 at 3 cm gives 3.78 sigma in simulation. R3 gives up to about 4.5 sigma but its ageing compliance is unknown, so R1 may not be the best allowed option.
